thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 — Julian Labs (private VPC) high error rate on /v1/generate; NLB target group returning 502s. Page sent to @maya_oncall and @leo_netops.

maya_oncall: acknowledging, I'm on it. tagging @irene_se for customer comms. putting a bridge up.

leo_netops: looking at NLB healthchecks — target group tg-julian-prod shows 60% unhealthy across two AZs. health check failures: connection timeout then 502.

maya_oncall: can you paste the latest target health events?

leo_netops: ```
> 2026-03-17T14:02:31Z target i-0abc123 unhealthy, reason=Health checks failed (tcp timeout)
> 2026-03-17T14:05:02Z target i-0abc123 unhealthy, reason=502 from backend
> 2026-03-17T14:07:10Z target i-0def456 unhealthy, reason=502 from backend
```

irene_se: customer reports ~40% of API calls failing, some retries succeed. Julian's SE (julian_cust_se) confirms they're seeing increased latency and downstream job failures. They're worried about data loss.

julian_cust_se: confirming, jobs hitting our ingest endpoint are failing intermittently. we routed traffic to backup only for some tenants; still seeing errors. do you have ETA?

sam_sre: quick hypothesis — healthchecks flipping due to a recent security group change blocking the NLB health-check source or internal probe IPs. also saw a spike in connection resets from the runtime around the same minute the SG rule was tightened.

leo_netops: checking SG audit: rule sg-07a9d recently had inbound 443 tightened to a narrow CIDR at 13:58 UTC (PR #4821). previous rule allowed Redwood-probes 52.12.0.0/16. new rule removed that.

maya_oncall: that would explain healthchecks. Julian's NLB probes come from our probe CIDR. can we temporarily reopen the SG for healthcheck CIDR?

leo_netops: I can patch SG now to add back 52.12.0.0/16 on 443 for the target subnet. Applying change and will monitor.

deploy-bot: action logged — inbound SG rule added to sg-07a9d: allow 52.12.0.0/16:443 by leo_netops at 2026-03-17T14:12:05Z.

sam_sre: after SG change, also increase NLB target group healthy threshold and interval to reduce flapping while we observe: set healthy threshold 3, interval 10s. I'm ready to apply.

leo_netops: applying target group config now. aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=slow-start.duration-seconds,Value=30; Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30

maya_oncall: monitoring metrics: 5xx rate dropping but not to zero yet. backend runtime traces show fewer resets.

irene_se: I told Julian's team the immediate mitigation is adding back probe CIDR and we are changing TG health-policy. asked them to hold off on their own config changes until we stabilize.

julian_cust_se: thanks — they confirmed they didn't change anything on their side during the window. customer asks for root cause and a longer-term fix.

sam_sre: long-term fix options: 1) add a pre-approved healthcheck rule in tenant onboarding (allowlist our probe CIDRs), 2) switch to health checks from within tenant VPC via cross-account probe, or 3) add a small TCP proxy in the tenant subnet that terminates checks and forwards to runtime. I'll draft recommended approach.

prashant_pm: please include estimated timelines and a low-risk rollout plan. customer is enterprise and wants a change window.

leo_netops: health back to normal across both AZs. target group healthy count returned to full at 14:18 UTC.

maya_oncall: marking incident as mitigated for now. keeping P1 until 1h steady state. starting 1h watch. handoff in 30m to next oncall @leo_netops.

irene_se: I'll send a brief incident update to Julian: summary, mitigation, ask for their maintenance window for a permanent rule, and offer a postmortem.

julian_cust_se: appreciate the quick response. please include the exact SG diffs and timestamps so our security team can reconcile.

sam_sre: noted — I'll attach SG revision diffs and the NLB healthcheck event log in the postmortem.

maya_oncall: oncall handoff in 30m. if errors resurge, page P1. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

leo_netops: taking over monitor at 14:42 UTC. will escalate if any more flapping.

deploy-bot: incident-bot: status change recorded: mitigated -> monitoring by maya_oncall at 2026-03-17T14:20:00Z.

maya_oncall: closing bridge; leaving channel open for PM follow-up and postmortem notes.

sam_sre: follow-up action items: 1) create onboarding checklist item to include probe CIDR allowlist (owner: eng-platform), 2) propose cross-account probe design (owner: eng-runtime), 3) draft customer-facing postmortem (owner: irene_se).

irene_se: will draft postmortem and send to @prashant_pm for review before sending to customer.

julian_cust_se: confirmed they are seeing no errors now. thanks again.

maya_oncall: final note: incident closed to monitoring; will reopen if metrics exceed thresholds. good job team.
